scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I should kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. We've been living together for two years, and we moved to our current apartment a year ago. The main reason we moved was because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy without roommates. That worked out well until J ran into some financial trouble. She didn't pay rent for two months, which caused some issues with her roommates. Eventually, she got the money from her family to pay off the rent and asked us to let her move in with us until the end of January. Her uncle was supposed to pick her up and take her out of state, but it seems like she's not really planning to go. Instead, she's staying in New York. My girlfriend, L, isn't confrontational, so she didn't oppose J moving in for free. Now, J has been with us for about four months. She doesn't have a job and only sometimes helps with cooking. She comes home to sleep after partying with her friends, and our place has become a hangover den. Because of the current situation, the job J had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. But that doesn't stop her from going out every other night to parties, which is concerning because if she gets sick from being reckless, it could affect us too. I want J out, but I'm really conflicted because it's her sister. I don't think L would be happy if I spoke to J about it, even though L also wants J out. I don't want to seem like a jerk, but it's gotten to the point where I might have to take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I've been trying to get L to talk to her, but she hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. So, the question is: Would I be within my rights to kick her out? Should I do it? Let me think through this step by step. First, legally, can I kick her out? Well, we're in an apartment that we rent, right? So, if J is a roommate, she might be on the lease. If she's not on the lease, then technically, the landlord could evict her. But if she is on the lease, it's more complicated. I need to check the lease agreement to see if she's listed. If she's not, then the landlord can ask her to leave. If she is, then we might need to go through legal eviction processes, which can be time-consuming and expensive. But legally aside, morally, is it right to kick her out? She's family, but she's also causing a lot of problems. She's not contributing financially, she's not looking for a job, and her behavior is affecting our living situation. I want my home back, and I want to have peace of mind that our space is ours. On the other hand, she's in a tough spot financially. She had some issues with her previous roommates, and now she's stuck. Maybe she needs help finding a job or a place to live. But she's not taking responsibility for her actions, and that's frustrating. I also have to consider how this will affect my relationship with L. If I confront J, L might be upset with me. But if I don't, I'm stuck living with someone who's making our life miserable. It's a tough spot. Maybe I should talk to L about this. Even though she doesn't like confrontation, we need to make a decision together. If we both agree that J needs to leave, then we can approach her together. That way, it's not just me being the bad guy, and it's a joint decision. Alternatively, maybe we can set some boundaries. Like, J has to contribute financially or find a job within a certain timeframe. If she doesn't, then she has to leave. That gives her a chance to improve the situation, but also sets clear expectations. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe J can stay for a little while longer if she starts looking for a job or contributes in some way. But from what I understand, she's not doing that. She's just using our place as a hangout spot and a place to sleep after parties. Another angle is to think about our own well-being. We deserve a peaceful home, and having J here is affecting that. It's not fair to us, and we should prioritize our own needs. But it's hard because she's family, and we want to help, but not at the expense of our own happiness. I also need to consider the practical aspects. If J leaves, where will she go? She was supposed to move out of state with her uncle, but that didn't happen. Maybe we can help her find another place, but that's not our responsibility. We've already given her a place to stay, and now it's time for her to move on. In summary, while it's difficult because she's family, the situation is causing significant problems in our home. We need to set boundaries and prioritize our own well-being. It might be the right decision to ask her to leave, even if it's hard.
